questions.question: You could be known for one EPIC talent. What would you choose?

answers.text: Being crazy powerful at one thing
Leading a big group that gets better together
Combining unrelated skills into something useful
Seeing problems coming and deciding how situations unfold

questions.question: You're planning a weekend with friends. Rank how you'd go about it.

answers.text: Start the hangout asap and figure stuff out as you go
Stick to the basics, stuff you know everyone will like
Plan ahead so you're covered if something goes wrong
Put all the effort into one big activity instead of a bunch of small ones

questions.question: Do you like seeing results right away, or building up slowly over time?
Rank these deck styles from the one that sounds most like you to the least.

answers.text: Hit them early and fast and try to win before they're ready
Solid creatures and a few tricks, nothing flashy, just good cards
Answer everything they do and win later on
Set up a combo that wins the game out of nowhere

questions.question: Rank these from most interesting to least interesting.

answers.text: A team of creatures that gets stronger together
Magic effects that stick around and make everything you do better
Gadgets and inventions that give each other new abilities
Get a little bonus every time you play a land

questions.question: When you're working on something, do you like doing your own thing or being part of what everyone else is doing?
You've got a free afternoon and not much money. What sounds best?

answers.text: Blow it all on one amazing thing right now
Buy a few smaller things that'll last a while
Keep some back in case plans change
Save it all toward one specific dream thing

questions.question: Rank these endings from most satisfying to least.

answers.text: A huge army just overwhelms everything
One legendary champion lands the final hit
A clever combo comes together and wins out of nowhere
I outlast everybody until they've got nothing left

questions.question: You get to pick one weird superpower. Which one?

answers.text: Your creatures keep getting permanently stronger
Your creatures can vanish and come back so you can use their abilities again
You can make extra little allies as you play
You get rewarded for casting spells back to back

questions.question: How much would you enjoy juggling a bunch of abilities that all interact with each other?
Would you rather your deck mostly build its own plan, or mostly mess with what your opponents are doing?
If you could win without attacking with creatures, how would you want to do it?

answers.text: Drain their life and gain it back for myself
Blast them with spells and direct damage
Empty out their deck so they can't draw anymore
Meet some weird condition on a card that just says I win

questions.question: Would you risk progress you've already made for a shot at something way bigger?
Pick up to two things you'd love to get out of a game.

answers.text: Feel powerful with big creatures and combat
Build something that keeps giving me stuff every turn
See an opponent's big move coming and shut it down
Pull off a combo nobody sees coming

questions.question: You're losing a game of commander and it's finally your turn. What sounds most like you?

answers.text: Throw everything I have into one huge turn to catch back up
Protect what I have left and slowly rebuild
Change my plan to whatever the board needs right now
Go for a risky play that wins it if it works and loses it if it doesn't

questions.question: Rank the type of army you would most like to lead.

answers.text: One unstoppable hero
A few enormous monsters
Many small allies working together
Ordinary fighters that grow stronger over time

questions.question: Would you rather focus on making one character extremely powerful or building a team of moderately strong characters?
Would you rather have a large group of weaker characters or a smaller group of stronger characters?
You're putting together a team of fantasy creatures. Which ability would you most want your team to have?

answers.text: They gradually grow stronger the longer they're around
They can summon more creatures to join the team
They become stronger when surrounded by others of their kind
They can combine their strength to create one powerful champion

questions.question: Which two abilities would you most want your deck to have?

answers.text: Use huge creatures to deal massive amounts of damage
Bring creatures back from the dead to use them again
Build machines and inventions that work together to become more powerful
Cast lots of spells to create different effects and combinations

questions.question: Which of these sounds the LEAST fun to play with?

answers.text: Gadgets and machines (artifacts) that just sit there and do stuff
Cards that stay out and quietly change the rules (enchantments)
Chaining a bunch of spells together in one turn
Creatures that leave and come back so their 'when I show up' thing happens again

questions.question: Would you rather build a team where every creature is the same type (all goblins, all zombies, whatever) and they boost each other, or just play the best creatures you can find?
How much would you enjoy controlling lots of creatures at once, each with their own abilities to keep track of?
questions.right: I enjoy having lots to manage

questions.question: Which of these sounds the LEAST fun to build around?

answers.text: Bringing creatures back from the graveyard
Sacrificing my own creatures for a bonus
Creatures that slowly get bigger over the whole game
Tons of tiny creature tokens

questions.question: Would you rather have creatures that start out strong or creatures that gradually grow stronger as you play?
Rank these ways of getting more use out of your creatures, from most to least appealing.

answers.text: Bring creatures back from the graveyard after they die
Sacrifice creatures to gain additional benefits or activate powerful effects
Temporarily exile creatures and bring them back to activate their abilities again
Create copies of creatures to use their abilities multiple times

questions.question: Would you rather keep your creatures alive to continue using them, or sacrifice them to gain an advantage?
Which of these ways of using cards sounds the most interesting to you?

answers.text: Use artifacts that work together to create stronger effects
Use enchantments that stay on the battlefield and provide ongoing benefits
Cast multiple spells that build off one another for bigger effects
Use creatures whose abilities activate when they enter the battlefield, then find ways to activate them again

questions.question: Would you rather play cards that have an immediate impact, or set up combinations of cards that generate more value every turn?
Which two of these additional benefits would you most want your deck to generate?

answers.text: Gain extra life as you play
Trigger special abilities whenever you play a land
Generate extra rewards each turn from cards and abilities working together
Create additional creatures to help build your army

questions.question: When playing a game with other people, which sounds the most fun?

answers.text: Making deals and convincing other players to work with me
Paying attention to what everyone is doing and adjusting my plans
Working toward my own goals without getting too involved in everyone else's plans
Getting everyone involved and creating fun moments together

questions.question: Would you rather focus on gaining life to stay in the game longer, or dealing damage to end the game faster?
Rank these setbacks from MOST frustrating to LEAST frustrating.

answers.text: Losing the creatures I spent turns developing
Running out of cards and useful choices
Falling far behind in the first few turns
Never drawing the cards I need to make my strategy work

questions.question: Would you be willing to help an opponent if you could negotiate something useful for yourself in return?
questions.right: I'd be open to making a deal

questions.question: You've got a bunch of mana left at the end of your turn (that's the stuff you spend to cast things). What do you wish you could do with it?

answers.text: Draw a bunch of extra cards
Bring a creature back from the graveyard
Pay for a huge creature that just smashes stuff
Hold it so i can stop whatever they do next

questions.question: Rank these ways of winning a game from MOST satisfying to LEAST satisfying.

answers.text: Defeat opponents by attacking with my creatures
Deal damage directly to opponents using spells and abilities
Gradually drain opponents' life while gaining life myself
Make opponents run out of cards in their libraries

questions.question: Would you rather overpower your opponents with strong plays, or gradually weaken their position until they struggle to fight back?
An opponent plays a powerful card that's going to cause problems for you. What would you rather do?

answers.text: Steal it and use it against them
Destroy it before it becomes a bigger problem
Keep it from being useful without necessarily getting rid of it
Focus on building my own board and try to overcome it

questions.question: How long do you want a game of Magic to last?
Which two ways of winning a game of Magic sound the most satisfying?

answers.text: Combine specific cards to pull off a powerful move that wins the game
Win instantly by meeting a special condition on one of my cards
Make my commander powerful enough to defeat opponents through its own combat damage
Build an army of creature tokens and overwhelm opponents with a massive attack

questions.question: Which of these cards would you be happiest to draw?

answers.text: One that always does something solid and reliable
A coin flip card: either amazing or it does nothing
One that's weak alone but incredible with the right other card
One that is just big and strong and does exactly what it says

questions.question: Making an opponent discard cards, or countering their spell right as they cast it. Is that your kind of fun?
Rank these cards from the one you'd be MOST excited to draw to the LEAST.

answers.text: A card that lets you sacrifice your own creatures for a big bonus
A creature that gains you life whenever you do certain things
A spell that lets you take control of an opponent's best creature
A card that does something cool every time you play a land

questions.question: Would you rather play cards that help everyone at the table (while you quietly steer things), or cards that just help you?
How fun would it be to play cards borrowed or stolen from your opponents?
Would you rather win because you outplayed everyone, or because you talked everyone into doing what you wanted?
Would you rather load your commander up with gear (equipment and auras) to make it a monster, or let your creatures grow on their own?
questions.left: Let them grow on their own

questions.question: Would you rather your commander (your deck's main character) win the game by attacking itself, or let your other cards do the winning while your commander helps out?
How frustrating is it when a deck needs several turns before it can do much?
Would you rather attack with your creatures every single turn even if it leaves you open, or keep some back to defend?
Would you rather have a tight serious game where everyone's trying their hardest, or a goofy chaotic one where wierd stuff happens?
Somebody casts a board wipe (a spell that destroys every creature, yours too). What would make you feel best?

answers.text: Bring all my creatures back from the graveyard
Have more creatures ready in my hand to play right away
Shrug it off and build something totally different
Stop the spell before it even happens

questions.question: Rank the qualities that make a deck appealing to you.

answers.text: A straightforward strategy that is easy to operate
Lots of technical choices and intricate decisions
Wild swings and unpredictable outcomes
Reliable plans with opportunities to adapt

questions.question: Would you rather stick to one game plan the whole game, or switch it up depending on what's happening?
How much do you enjoy choosing when to act based on what other players do?
Would you rather lands just be lands, or build a deck around lands that make fun stuff happen when you play them?
How appealing is a strategy that sometimes does very little before one huge payoff?
Would you rather play a spell that does its thing once and is gone, or a card that stays out and quietly changes the rules (like 'all your creatures get +1/+1' or 'nobody can attack you for free')?
Would you rather play a deck you can explain in one sentence, or one that takes a whole paragraph to explain how it wins?
Would you rather play a deck that does a bit of everything pretty well, or one that goes all in on one thing?
